To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an auto-encoder based model that learns a healthy brain distribution and uses a simple constraint on the latent space to improve lesion detection in brain MRI.

1) the proposed constrained adversarial autoencoder (CAA) outperforms state-of-the-art auto-encoder based approaches for unsupervised lesion detection in brain MRI; 2) CAA outperforms the supervised approaches in terms of AUPR and AUC; and 3) the proposed constraint is effective in reducing the effect of the latent space inconsistency.

(a) we can detect lesions in brain MRI in an unsupervsied manner using auto-encoders, (b) the constraint we introduce helps the auto-encoder model learn better latent representation of healthy brain MRI and (c) this in turn improves the detection of lesion regions.

unsupervised learning of data distribution of healthy brain MRI to detect lesion regions in an image.
developing an unsupervised approach to detect lesions in brain MRI.
